title: Rollout microtome checklist and watchlist — March 2026 (notes)
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a lightweight, operational-first release plan using a ‘microtome’ slicing approach — cut the release into many very thin, orthogonal slices (by customer cohort, region, and model-variant) so we can observe signal early and limit blast radius. This doc is a working notes + checklist for the week-of and the 72 hours after rollout. Treat as living; add runbook IDs and final traffic percentages once the rollout window is locked.

High-level goals:
- Deliver feature X (model routing adjustments + cache policy change) with minimal user-visible regression.
- Validate latency, error, and cost signals at each microtome step.
- Keep MTTR under 30 minutes for major regressions via automated rollback lanes.

What ‘microtome’ means here (operationally):
- Split traffic by: feature-flag cohort (A/B), region (us-east, eu-west), customer tier (free/paid), and model variant (v1-q4, v1-q8).
- Each slice targets <= 0.5% of global traffic initially; increases follow a gated cadence.
- Each increase requires green on specified telemetry windows (5m p50/p99, 15m errors, 1hr quality sample).

Preflight checklist (T-72 to T-1 hours):
- [ ] Finalize rollout matrix (slice id, initial pct, expand increments). Owner: Aisha.
- [ ] Smoke tests: end-to-end generation for three representative prompts per slice. Owner: Jun.
- [ ] Telemetry hooks in place and validated: latency histograms, request errors, token-cost metrics, KV cache hit ratio. Owner: SRE.
- [ ] Canary job script checked into repo with dry-run flag. Owner: Marcus.
- [ ] Alert thresholds loaded into Ops channel (see "Watch signals" below). Owner: Oncall SRE.
- [ ] Product release notes draft and customer-facing caveats reviewed. Owner: Product.
- [ ] Communication plan: #release-microtome Slack channel created (pinned links to Confluence, runbooks, and PagerDuty). Owner: Release lead.
- [ ] Backup plan: suspend autoscaling burst windows and reserve a rollback capacity pool (label: rollback-pool). Owner: Infra.

Day-of rollout cadence (T0 = 10:00 UTC):
- T0 + 00:00: deploy control-plane config (no traffic change). Verify agent configs and model pinning.
- T0 + 00:10: enable slice 001 (region: us-east, cohort: internal-canaries) -> 0.25% traffic. Observability window: 10m.
- T0 + 00:20: if green, increase slice 001 -> 1.0%. Run sample-quality eval (sample id: SQ-001).
- T0 + 01:00: enable slice 002 (paid-tier, eu-west) -> 0.5%. Observability window: 15m.
- Gate rule: any slice increase requires: p99 latency delta < 20% or < 100ms absolute, error-rate delta < 0.1% absolute, no downstream 5xx spike. If gate fails, roll back the slice to previous percentage and open an incident.

Watch signals and thresholds (primary):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per slice. Alert if p99 increases >20% and absolute p99 > 700ms.
- Errors: 4xx/5xx per-minute rate. Alert if 5xx > 0.05% of requests in 5m window.
- Quality regressions: sampling eval score drop >10% vs baseline on held prompt set.
- Cost: tokens-per-request delta > +15% sustained for 30m.
- Cache: KV cache hit ratio drops > 5% -> investigate changed cache keys from config change.
- Downstream dependencies: DB tail latencies, rate-limits, and GPU OOM events.

Rollback ladder (fastest-first):
1) Scale down offending slice to 0%. Runbook: RB-FAST-01. Owner: release lead.
2) If rollback not resolving, flip global emergency feature flag to previous stable. Runbook: RB-GLOBAL-01.
3) If persistent infra degradation, activate rollback-pool and shift traffic to dedicated stable variant. Owner: SRE + Infra.

Role-specific quick checklist (day-of):
- Release lead: monitor #release-microtome, approve slice increases, call incident if gate fails.
- SRE oncall: watch SLO dashboard and execute RB runbooks; keep PagerDuty on.
- Infra: ensure GPU pool headroom and watch quota alerts.
- Product: monitor customer support queue and prepare one-paragraph customer note if noise increases.
- Dev: ready to ship hotfixes; keep PRs small and trunk-based.

72-hour post-rollout plan:
- T+4h: automated regression sampling across 1000 sessions, compare model-quality metrics.
- T+24h: daily traffic expansion review and decide on final 7-day ramp schedule.
- T+48h: small customer outreach for paid customers who saw changed routing.
- T+72h: retro notes: what signals caught regressions, any manual steps used, timeline of mitigations.

Observability artifacts to attach (fill-in links before go):
- Dashboard: RE/rollout/microtome-ops-dash (TODO link).
- Sampling job: jobs/release/sq-001 (link to job config).
- Error log queries: saved-searches/release-5xx-microtome.

Release notes (customer-facing draft) — Feature X (model routing + cache policy)
- Short blurb: We’re rolling out smarter routing that prefers low-latency model variants for short prompts, and updated KV cache semantics to reuse aligned prefix caches. This reduces median latency for common prompts and lowers token usage for cached conversations.
- Why you might see changes: Some sessions may be routed to a different model-variant early in rollout; this can slightly alter generation style for affected prompts.
- Impact window: progressive rollout over 3 days; any negative impact will be mitigated by our rollback lanes.
- Suggested action for customers: If you have strict deterministic output needs, pin to the existing model variant in the Console (instructions link).
- Known issues: under rare conditions long-chain context prompts may see higher cost for first request after cache invalidation; fix tracked in JIRA-RELEASE-9944.

Open tasks and TODOs before finalizing:
- [ ] Insert final dashboard links (Aisha).
- [ ] Confirm infra quota reservation numbers and attach infra runbook (Marcus).
- [ ] Add customer communication template for a potential escalated note (Product).
- [ ] Finalize canary sample set (Jun).

Quick retrospective prompts (post-mortem template snippets):
- Timeline: short bullets for each slice increase and observed metrics.
- Detection: what caught the first signal? noisy alerts, manual checks, or downstream reports?
- Mitigation: what was the quickest effective action?
- Root cause: config drift, model artifact, or traffic misclassification?
- Improvement items: telemetry gaps, automation gaps, docs to update.

Notes-to-self (fragments, keep here):
- consider adding a synthetic load job that mimics token distribution of prod to stress cache changes prior to any traffic shifts.
- think about a mute window for low-priority alerts during scheduled increases to avoid paging noise; but keep paging for blockers.

End of notes.

Revision history:
- 2026-03-03: initial outline (Aisha).
- 2026-03-07: added rollback ladder and detailed gates (Jun).
- 2026-03-10: updated watch thresholds and post-rollout schedule (Aisha).
